evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.controller.ts: @Controller('enrolments') and @Post() / @Post('withdrawals') are NestJS routing decorators from @nestjs/common, which belong in the presentation layer.
enrol(@Body() dto: EnrolDto): Promise<Enrolment> passes the request straight to this.enrolmentsService.enrol(courseId, dto.studentEmail), so the controller makes no business decision.
withdraw(...) calls this.enrolmentsService.withdraw(...) and only wraps the boolean it gets back in { refund }. The refund decision is made by the application layer.
constructor(private readonly enrolmentsService: EnrolmentsService) injects an application-layer service, which is dependency wiring presentation is allowed.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the presentation layer and contains only presentation work. It uses NestJS routing decorators (@Controller, @Post, @Body), receives an application-layer DTO and passes both calls on to the injected EnrolmentsService, which belongs to the application layer. It returns either a domain Enrolment or a simple response object. It has no business rule, calculation or decision of its own. The refund value comes from the service and is only wrapped in the response. The constructor injects a service from a layer that presentation may depend on, so it is ordinary dependency wiring. No candidate flags were raised, and checking the source found no misplaced responsibilities.
